blogs.title: Demystifying eXponential Gating – The Secret Tool for Memory Revision
blogs.description: This post explains how eXponential Gating expands an LSTM’s ability to rewrite its own memories on the fly. Using an everyday grocery‑list analogy, we show how traditional sigmoid gates lock earlier items in place while exponential gates allow the model to “overwrite” old facts when newer data arrives—solving one of LSTMs’ classic weaknesses while remaining fully trainable.

blogs.title: Matrix Memories Made Simple – How xLSTMs Store Millions of Tokens Efficiently
blogs.description: We break down the mLSTM’s matrix‑memory mechanism that uses simple outer‑product updates (covariance rule) to turn each recurrent cell into an associative cache similar to Fast Weight Programmers. Think of it like a librarian automatically creating cross‑references between books; no extra parameters are needed, yet storage jumps from a single scalar value to full d×d matrices that power ten‑to‑hundred‑parameter language models.

blogs.title: The New Residual Backbone – Why xLSTMs Beat Self‑Attention at Scale
blogs.description: Explore how sLSTM and mLSTM are folded into residual blocks via pre/post up‑projection schemes that mirror Transformer and State‑Space attention schemas. We contrast linear time complexity versus quadratic cost, detail how mLSTM parallelizes like FlashAttention while sLSTM stays efficient thanks to CUDA kernels, and see why this architecture delivers stronger results on real language benchmarks.

blogs.title: "Scaling Beyond Attention" – Why xLSTMs Outperform Transformers When Size Matters
blogs.description: Summarizing large‑scale experiments from the paper, this post shows that billions of parameter xLSTMs beat GPT–3 sized Transformers and State‑Space Models on validation perplexity while scaling nicely according to power‐law laws. We cover longer‑context robustness (16384 tokens), inference speed due its constant memory footprint, and implications for deploying high‑capacity models on edge devices or reinforcement learning agents.
